- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment volatility.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0), model overreacts; dampen forecast slope by 15–30% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high and price is trending down; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% if sentiment >0.7 and price declines >2%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 10–15 days of high prices; apply downward bias of 1–4% per day if sentiment <0.5 and price >mean+2σ.
- If sentiment is stable (±0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model tends to lag by 2–5 days; forecast should be adjusted to match recent 7-day moving average.
